Earlier this year, Apple closed part of the Apple Park Visitor Center, saying it was to "improve our store."

That space has now reopened, and the biggest change is that Apple has removed the augmented reality experience that let visitors use a special iPad to view Apple Park.

When the Apple Park Visitor Center opened to the public in 2017, Apple described the AR experience like this:

Using augmented reality technology, a three-dimensional model of the campus comes to life, inviting guests to explore Apple Park in an immersive and engaging way. Visitors can learn about the world's largest naturally ventilated building structure and see one of the largest on-site solar installations in the world. Visitors can also choose to lift the entire roof of the building to peek at the collaborative workspace layout inside.

Before this change, the Apple Park Visitor Center was divided into three areas: the AR exhibit, a traditional Apple Store, and a cafe.

Apple has now retired the AR exhibit and converted it into an extension of the traditional Apple Store. As MacRumors noted, this includes a wall of Avenues accessory displays and redesigned tables showcasing Apple products.

The rest of the Apple Park Visitor Center, including the cafe, remains unchanged.

9to5Mac's take

The AR experience at the Apple Park Visitor Center was certainly unique, but nine years on, it seems the space could be put to good use in other ways.

I had hoped Apple wouldn't just turn it into a regular retail store, but at least the cafe is still there as a distinctive element of the Apple Park Visitor Center.
